annotations.text:
Revision 2 (8 Sept, evening): you liked Direction A and asked for more dimension and a more modern typeface.

Changed: a four-level elevation system (void, panel, object, glass) with lit edges and real shadows; a perspective stage floor and a light from above on every screen; recessed fields, raised buttons; the stage-mode pitch view is now a runway with depth; type is now Geist + Geist Mono (two alternatives on the Type options board to the right).

Unchanged: palette, the living-light rule, the ten answers from the interview, and the two alternate directions below.

The six screens are static mockups of the flow a first user takes: sign in, voice check, the setlist home, a song's key and mix, stage mode while singing, and the result.

All numbers, note names, dates, venue and song titles are sample content, not measurements: the 94 score and its section scores, +6 and +22 cents, B minus 3, 62 %, minus 18 dB, 1:48 / 3:54, and "up 6 from Sunday".

Pick a direction, not a polish level. If B or C wins, the six screens get redrawn in it before anything is built. If A wins, the next step is your go on the foundation plan; the first build then implements these tokens and components.
Three pairings, same words. My pick is the first (Geist): current, even, precise, and its mono lines up with the text face. Say which one you want and every screen is redrawn in it.
